summary: A correctness patch: the script cache, constant tables, nested modules, match-arm code generation, and unsigned comparisons are fixed.

highlights.title: Script cache runs keep stdin
highlights.text: A warm script-cache hit ran the cached program with closed input, so a second run of a program that reads from the terminal saw nothing; the --no-cache and --jit flags were also ignored on that path. Cached runs now inherit stdin and the flags are honored.

highlights.title: Constant tables with strings and structs
highlights.text: Module-level constant arrays of strings or structs were not materialized correctly: struct fields read as zero and string lengths returned garbage. They are now real constant globals, and integer tables are unchanged.

highlights.title: Nested modules and same-name payload types
highlights.text: A module nested under another module (for example a package tests module importing its package) saw none of the parent module's exports. A struct type sharing a name with an enum variant was also built as the enum and produced broken code; the type now wins inside its module.

highlights.title: Match arms and unsigned comparisons
highlights.text: An uninitialized local assigned inside match arms could crash or read garbage. An inline comparison of a module-qualified unsigned call result misread values with the top bit set. Constant-valued match arms never matched and always fell through to the default arm. All three are fixed.

highlights.title: Doctor version checks
highlights.text: The doctor no longer warns when the standard library's own release line differs from the compiler's patch version, and tag-shaped standard-library pins are not compared as versions.

highlights.title: Compile-phase timings
highlights.text: Setting XIOM_TIMINGS=1 prints per-phase compile times to stderr (parse, check, borrow, codegen), for profiling builds and benchmarks.

known_issues: LZ4 block compression can read an empty result in some larger programs; the cause is isolated and scheduled for the next minor release.

The contract verifier emits malformed SMT for some obligations (undeclared symbols, duplicate named expressions), so those checks report unknown instead of proving; scheduled for the next minor release.
